transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees (Redwood): Sophie Tran (AE), Marco Diaz (SE), Alex Low (SE)
Attendees (Equinox): Priya Malhotra (Head of Security), Daniel Park (Platform Eng), Marta Ruiz (IT Ops), Tom Ellis (Compliance)

Summary: Quick security review focused on how Equinox will integrate SSO (SAML), user provisioning (SCIM), and map their least-privilege RBAC. Covered audit log retention and KMS options for a Dedicated/pilot deployment. Agreed next steps for pilot kickoff and doc handoffs.

00:00 Sophie (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got Priya and team from Equinox, thanks for making time. we're going to run through SAML/SCIM angles, role mapping and the compliance pieces that usually come up.
00:14 Priya (Equinox): Thanks Sophie, yeah we want to validate that the auth flow meets our infosec checklist before we spin up anything; SOC 2 is table stakes for us and then we have some EU data residency concerns.
00:30 Marco (Redwood SE): Totally, we'll start high level and then dig into specific endpoints. Quick question — are you using Okta or Azure AD today for your IdP?
00:45 Daniel (Equinox): We're mainly on Okta for workforce SSO, and we have some apps in Azure AD but Okta is the primary. We do SCIM for a couple internal tools already.
00:58 Sophie: Great, Okta is the common path. For SAML we support standard SAML 2.0 metadata exchange, and we have a hosted metadata endpoint we can provide or you can upload ours into Okta.
01:12 Marta (Equinox): One thing — can you confirm if the SAML assertions contain groups or role attributes? We want to avoid mapping everything to admin by default.
01:25 Alex (Redwood): Good call. We support mapping an assertion to role ids; we typically recommend using a groups attribute with the minimum set of groups and then use SCIM to provision fine-grained role bindings. There is a sample mapping in the quickstart doc.
01:40 Priya: How about provisioning latency and eventual consistency? If I remove a user in Okta, how long until they're deprovisioned in Redwood? We have a 15-minute SLA internally for critical revokes.
01:54 Marco: With SCIM push provisioning, we see deltas almost immediately, usually sub-30 seconds on our hosted offering; for Dedicated or Private deployments we give a configurable sync interval and you can configure immediate web-hook style deltas for critical revocations. But we'll need to ensure outbound connectivity from your VPC if you choose private/piped mode.
02:13 Tom (Compliance): Are audit logs immutable? We need tamper-evidence for SOC 2 audit.
02:23 Marco: Our audit logs are append-only in the control plane, and for Dedicated we can ship logs to your logging endpoint (S3/CloudWatch/GCP Logging) with integrity checks. We can also enable signed digest rotation for an additional chain-of-trust. I'll put the details in the SOC2 bundle we send.
02:40 Priya: Excellent. On encryption — we are required to bring our own keys for some workloads. Can Redwood integrate with external KMS or HSM?
02:51 Alex: Yes; we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS) and we have an HSM tile for on-prem private deployments. For Hosted you can use envelope encryption with a customer KMS as well. There are a few caveats around key rotation windows and how we cache keys in the runtime — we can document operational playbooks.
03:15 Daniel: If we use our KMS for token encryption, where are the keys stored and who has admin visibility? We need separation of duty.
03:26 Marco: Keys remain in your KMS and Redwood never stores raw master keys. On run-time we use ephemeral wrapping keys and a short-lived cache on the node for performance; control plane metadata is encrypted. We can scope access so that only a small set of operators (your service account) have decrypt permission.
03:45 Priya: Data residency — we have EU patients and HIPAA-adjacent data. We need guarantees about where tokenized context and logs live.
03:58 Sophie: For Dedicated and Private deployments you can pin the region; for Hosted we have region-aware routing and we can restrict tenant data to EU regions, we also have contractual addendum for data residency. For PHI and HIPAA-like constraints, Private VPC or on-prem is typically recommended.
04:20 Marta: On RBAC — we have a complex role matrix: clinical_viewer, clinical_editor, billing_admin, engineering_infra, etc. We don't want to replicate 40 roles in the inference layer, but we do need separation for billing and PII access. Thoughts on role slicing?
04:38 Marco: A common pattern is role-slicing: map coarse-grained roles in the IdP and use SCIM to provision scoped permissions in Redwood. For example, clinical_viewer can be provisioned with read-only data access and token redaction flags, while billing_admin gets usage/export privileges. We also support permission inheritance and deny-lists to enforce least privilege.
04:58 Daniel: Is there support for attribute-based access in addition to role-based? Like department=oncology and location=eu influencing access?
05:10 Alex: We do support attributes in assertion and they can be used in policy rules. It's more advanced, but the policy engine supports attribute conditions for route-level access and dataset scoping. We'll include examples.
05:26 Priya: For auditing, auditors ask for a play-by-play of who accessed what prompts and outputs — retention windows vary. What retention can you offer?
05:38 Marco: Logs retention is configurable per-tenant; hosted default is 90 days but can be extended. For Dedicated we can support 1 year+, and you can archive logs to your storage. Note that for retention of model outputs we offer redaction and hashing options for PII and a policy-driven TTL.
05:58 Tom: Do you support exportable audit reports in a standard schema? Our auditors like CSV plus a JSON LEEF-like format.
06:10 Marco: Yes, we can export in CSV and a structured JSON schema. We also have integrations to SIEM through push export. I'll share the schema file.
06:20 Sophie: Quickly, on SOC 2/ISO — we have an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II, and are working toward ISO 27001; both artifacts are in the SOC2 bundle and ISO summary.
06:33 Priya: Can you confirm encryption at rest for ephemeral cache and model artifacts?
06:40 Alex: Model artifacts are encrypted at rest in object storage and the runtime caches are encrypted using node-level disk encryption; ephemeral KV still lives in memory but we have guardrails to scrub. For added isolation we can use dedicated hosts.
06:56 Daniel: A slightly tricky item — we have machine accounts that call the inference API from our backend, and occasionally developers spin up service tokens. We need short TTLs and fine-grained service roles.
07:10 Sophie: We support short-lived tokens via our token service and you can mint scoped tokens with TTLs as low as 5 minutes. There's an automated rotation flow for CI/CD integrations. Also we support role-bound API keys with limited method access.
07:28 Marta: Are there rate-limits per-role or per-token? We need to ensure billing separation.
07:36 Marco: Yes rate-limiting is configurable by route, model, and token. For Dedicated pilots we often provision separate capacity to ensure billing separation and predictable QoS.
07:50 Priya: For SCIM, what attributes do you require? Are emails immutable keys, or do you prefer externalId?
08:02 Alex: We prefer an immutable externalId if you have it; email can change. SCIM schema we support is standard but we recommend externalId to avoid conflicts. We'll attach an example payload in the quickstart.
08:18 Daniel: On provisioning failure modes — what happens if SCIM returns 500 or Okta mis-syncs — do you have a fail-closed or fail-open pattern?
08:30 Marco: By default we fail-safe to deny access if provisioning metadata is missing for an API call relying on RBAC. For session-level SSO we still allow re-auth via SAML if the user exists in the IdP, but for deprovisioning we prioritize security. We can tailor the behavior for pilot to be more forgiving during ramp.
08:52 Tom: Any third-party sub-processors we should be aware of?
08:58 Sophie: We maintain a list of subprocessors (CDN, object storage, telemetry). That's in the SOC2 bundle. We also support subprocessors disallow lists for Enterprise contracts.
09:10 Priya: Ok that's good. Let's talk about the pilot — we want to do an initial pilot with 50 users and production-like traffic to validate deprovisioning, audit trails, and the RBAC mapping. Timeline target is two weeks. Is that feasible?
09:26 Marco: Yes, we can do a two-week pilot. We'll propose Dedicated pilot capacity with limited ingress. We will need your IdP admin to exchange metadata, a CSV of your role mapping, and a sandbox project in your cloud if you want logs archived to your bucket.
09:44 Sophie: I'll follow up with an email listing required artifacts. We'll also include a checklist for SOC/ISO point-of-contacts.
10:00 Priya: One more question — does Redwood support SCIM group-to-role sync instead of per-user provisioning? That would simplify our lifecycle.
10:10 Alex: Yes group-based provisioning is supported; that's often the simpler pattern for larger orgs. You can map groups to roles during the SCIM config.
10:22 Daniel: Any gotchas around SAML NameID formats? We're using transient in some apps and emailAddress in others.
10:33 Marco: For Redwood we recommend persistent or emailNameID; transient can cause session reconciliation issues. If you must use transient we have a reconciliation layer but it's more complex.
10:47 Priya: For encryption key rotation — what are the operational windows and can we coordinate?
10:53 Alex: Rotation can be scheduled and we support rolling rotations with zero downtime if you use KMS-backed keys. We'll provide an ops playbook.
11:05 Marta: Are there any logs that include prompt text or model outputs by default? We have to be careful with PHI.
11:15 Marco: By default request/response may show traces for debugging but we have redaction and hashing features. You can enable automatic PII detection and redact or replace tokens in logs prior to storage. That's strongly recommended for PHI environments.
11:32 Sophie: Alright to recap next steps — Redwood sends SOC bundle + SAML/SCIM quickstart; Marco shares SAML metadata and SCIM examples; Equinox shares role CSV and IdP admin contact; schedule pilot kickoff week of 11/29.
11:48 Priya: Sounds good. We'll get the role CSV to you by 11/24 and loop in our Okta admin.
11:58 Sophie: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifacts.
12:05 Meeting end.
